identity.title: Millimeter Spectral Indices and Dust Trapping By Planets in Brown Dwarf Disks

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present 3 mm photometric observations carried out with the IRAM/Plateau de Bure Interferometer (PdBI) of three BD disks in the Taurus star forming region, which have been observed with ALMA at 0.89 mm.
We took the 0.89 mm measurements from (cite: ward2017), where the details of the ALMA observations can be found.

question.value: Can dust trapping by an embedded planet in a brown dwarf disk explain the low millimeter spectral indices observed in BD disks?

evidence.quote: In this paper, we explore whether dust trapping by a massive planet (which may not form in the disk) can lead to low millimeter spectral indices as observed in BD disks.
Project number #2012.1.00743.S

bands.value: ALMA Band 7 (339 GHz, 0.89 mm); PdBI 3.0 mm (100 GHz)

evidence.quote: which were observed with ALMA in Band 7 ($\sim$0.89 mm, 339 GHz)
The most compact configuration of five antennas was used to have the maximum sensitivity possible, with a longest baseline of 97 m.
The obtained resolution was around $\sim$3$''$.8$\times$4$''$.8 for all the targets.

max_recoverable_scale.value: flux regions well within the maximum recoverable scale for ALMA

evidence.quote: The sizes of the regions used to extract the fluxes was well within the maximum recoverable scale for all the ALMA observations.
The total time on source was 4.3 hr for J043903, 3.9 hr for J044148, and 3.6 hr for J043814.
The observations were made on 2014 July 23, 26, and 31.
